name: Meta Kuna Data Center
developer: Meta Platforms (utility customer of record: Brisbie, LLC)
status_note: Serving traffic as of September 2026, according to a Meta executive’s post reported by Baxtel. Announced February 2022 with about 100 permanent jobs.
tax: BoiseDev describes Meta as eligible for the 63-3622VV sales tax exemption. 2025 Senate committee minutes record conflicting testimony on whether the Tax Commission granted it. No public record shows the amount. Our note.
power: Special contract with Idaho Power under the name Brisbie, LLC, approved by the PUC May 11, 2023 (case IPC-E-21-42). Meta says it added 645 MW of new renewable supply in Ada County to match its use. Neither Meta nor Idaho Power has published the site’s load in megawatts.
water: Meta transferred about 2.5 million gallons a day of farm water rights to the City of Kuna and runs the site on a separate system. Expected summer peak use is just under 2 million gallons a day, BoiseDev reported.
local: Inside the Kuna East urban renewal district, created in 2022.

name: Gemstone Technology Park
developer: Diode Ventures, a Black & Veatch subsidiary (applicant: Gemstone Technology Park LLC)
status_note: Kuna approved the rezone April 1, 2025, on a tie broken by the mayor. Neighbors sued; a district judge denied their petition in May 2026 and they appealed to the Idaho Supreme Court in June. No hearing date was set as of August. Design review is still ahead.
tax: Could qualify for 63-3622VV, BoiseDev reported. No record shows a claim.
power: Idaho Power has completed a feasibility study; the developer says it will pay all interconnection upgrades. No PUC contract found. The Idaho Conservation League estimates 600 to 800 MW; the developer has not published a figure.
water: Plans to move three irrigation water rights, about 1.63 million gallons a day, to industrial use through a pending Idaho Department of Water Resources transfer, with on-site treatment and reinjection.
local: The developer offered about $40 million to Kuna’s fire district, police and schools.

name: T5 Data Centers Nampa
developer: T5 Data Centers, for one unnamed tenant
status_note: Nampa’s planning commission approved a conditional use permit in August 2025 to convert an existing building in Park 84. Whether it is operating is not reported.
power: About 2.25 MW at first, rising to 8.25 MW, BoiseDev reported. Another outlet put the first stage at 2.5 MW.
water: Air-cooled; the developer compared water use to one or two homes.

name: Rhea Data, Blacks Creek
developer: Rhea Data, a subsidiary of Nevada-based Arevia Power
size_note: About 4 million sq ft on roughly 3,200 to 3,750 acres
status_note: Applied to the Bureau of Land Management’s Four Rivers Field Office to use public land south of Kuna-Mora Road. The BLM expects to open formal environmental review with public comment around the end of 2026.
power: 600 MW of computing, per the applicant. An on-site gas plant of about 450 MW appears in the applicant’s early filings; the BLM has not confirmed the energy plan. Idaho Power says Rhea is not in its load forecast and any service would need PUC review.
local: Federal land, so the BLM decides, not a city or county. Boise’s mayor called selling public land for mega data centers “shortsighted.”
unconfirmed: Acreage varies by outlet (3,226; 3,200; about 3,700; about 3,750). The gas plant size comes from one outlet’s reading of the filings.

name: Bennett Ranch Industrial Campus
size_note: About 3.4 million sq ft in four buildings
status_note: A concept was dropped off at City Hall on October 20, 2026. No land-use application has been filed. A week later the city adopted an emergency moratorium on data center applications.
power: The concept includes its own power generation and backup power. Size not stated.
water: Closed-loop cooling proposed. A 2005 agreement may allow a city water connection, KIVI reported.
local: Data centers are not a permitted or conditional use in any Mountain Home zone, the mayor said. Emergency moratorium adopted October 27, 2026.

name: TerraVolt Campus
status_note: Announced options to buy 1,077 acres on October 30, 2026. Data centers are not a permitted use in Cassia County, so the project needs county zoning approval. Commissioners hold a public meeting November 10.
power: 240 MW of gas generation on site, separate from the grid, fed by the Williams Northwest Pipeline under a supply deal announced in May 2026.
water: The company says closed-loop or low-water cooling will be required of each site buyer.

name: Lex Developments AI campus (former Hoku plant)
status_note: Pocatello denied a conditional use permit in May 2026 and upheld the denial twice, most recently 3-2 on September 17. The developer petitioned the Sixth District Court for judicial review in late October, arguing no permit was needed in the industrial zone. It also says it plans to reapply; the council waived the usual one-year wait.
tax: Not reported. BoiseDev noted it could qualify for Idaho’s property tax cap for $1 billion-plus investments, a separate break.
power: An Idaho Power feasibility letter cites more than 100 MW by 2031. The developer has also said the site could host up to 300 MW of gas generation.
water: No wastewater figure was given to the city.
local: The Shoshone-Bannock Tribes and more than 80 speakers at the first hearing opposed it. Bannock County separately adopted a moratorium for unincorporated areas.

name: Idaho National Laboratory AI data center site
place: INL desert site, west of Idaho Falls
developer: U.S. Department of Energy, seeking private partners
status_note: DOE named INL one of four federal sites for private AI data centers in July 2025 and took applications through November 2025. We found no developer selection for INL; DOE has announced picks at Savannah River and Paducah. Separately, Aalo Atomics and Crusoe announced in July 2026 a small reactor-powered demonstration data center at INL for 2027.
power: DOE prefers new nuclear or geothermal power. The Aalo demonstration pairs a 10 MWe reactor with a modular data center.
water: DOE will not lend its federal water rights; developers must acquire Idaho water rights.
unconfirmed: Whether DOE has chosen an INL developer since August 2026.
